rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Israelites were punished immediately when they forgot, so believers ask God not to hold them accountable for forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: قاله الكلبي، وهو أن بني إسرائيل كانوا إذا نسوا شيئا عجلت لهم العقوبة بذلك، فأمر الله نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when religious law excuses forgetfulness, believers may still be taught to pray for pardon, as prophets and angels petition for things God will certainly grant.
rows.anchor: بأن ندعو بذلك، كما جاء في الدعاء: {قال رب احكم بالحق} [الأنبياء: 112]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here forgetting can mean abandoning an obligation; in 9:67, people abandon God's service and are left without reward.
rows.anchor: بمعنى: الترك، فيكون معنى قوله: {إن نسينا} أي: تركنا شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correct linguistic distinction is خطئ for intentional sin and أخطأ for failing to hit the right answer; Abu al-Haytham likewise distinguishes deliberate from accidental acts.
rows.anchor: الصحيح في اللغة: أن يقال: خطئ الرجل: إذا أثم، فهو خاطئ آثم. وأخطأ: إذا لم يصب الصواب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: If أخطأنا means an inadvertent slip, it shares the two explanations given for forgetfulness, including Al-Kalbi's account of immediate punishment for Israelites.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: قول الكلبي (¬1) والثاني: أنا تعبدنا بهذا الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication for pardon over inadvertent error is also a devotional prayer believers are instructed to make.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنا تعبدنا بهذا الدعاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats أخطأ and خطئ as two forms of one word, citing poetry; on this reading the verse asks pardon for deliberate sin.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: يقال: أخطأ وخطئ لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isr fundamentally conveys binding or attachment; it names burdens, covenants, and kin ties, supported by poetry and by the covenant called isr in 3:81.
rows.anchor: فالأصل في هذا الحرف الإصر بمعنى العطف، ثم يسمى الثقل والعهد إصرا لما فيهما من العطف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in reports from Al-Walibi, Ata, and Atiyya, and Mujahid, Qatada, Muqatil, Al-Suddi, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Farra say it means an unbearable covenant whose breach brought punishment on the Jews.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي وعطاء وعطية (¬1): يعنى: عهدا وميثاقا لا نطيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāqa is a verbal noun from iṭāqa, like ṭāʿa from iṭāʿa, and can stand in place of the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الطاقة: اسم من الإطاقة، كالطاعة (¬10) من الإطاعة، والجابة من الإجابة، وهي توضع موضع المصدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the petition asks God not to subject them to Hellfire, whose punishment no one can bear.
rows.anchor: أي: من العذاب، كأنهم سألوا الله تعالى أن لا يعذبهم بالنار، فإنه لا طاقة لأحد مع عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is a burden that is technically possible but onerous and painful; Arabs say they cannot bear someone's sight despite being physically able, as in 11:20.
rows.anchor: أي: ما يثقل علينا أداؤه، وإن كنا مطيقين له بعد التجشم وتحمل (¬1) المكروه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes explain Mawlana as our helper or protector, as in the verses calling God the believers' wali or mawla.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: أي: ناصرنا (¬3)، ومثله: {الله ولي الذين آمنوا} [البقرة: 257]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawla in the sense of aid derives from closeness and connection; wali and mawla are equivalent, as in God's being with the believers as their helper.
rows.anchor: ومعنى المولى: من النصرة، من ولي عليه، وولي منه: إذا اتصل به ولم ينفصل عنه

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus explains the Prophet's saying Whoever has me as his mawla, Ali is his mawla to mean whoever has me as his wali.
rows.anchor: قال يونس (¬7): أي: من كنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report calling Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam, and Ghifar God's and His Messenger's mawali means they are His allies; Al-Ajjaj's verse likewise uses mawali for allies of truth.
rows.anchor: أي: أولياء الله، وقال العجاج:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone joined to you and protected by your strength is your mawla; this explains calling paternal kin mawali, while poetry distinguishes allied clients from relatives and mawla can mean a guardian of one's affairs.
rows.anchor: وكل من انضم إليك فعز بعزك وامتنع بمنعتك (¬4)، فهو مولاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is our wali by helping us and by directing our affairs; the verb is wali, yali, wilayah, making Him wali and mawla.
rows.anchor: فمعنى قوله: أنت مولانا أي: أنت ولينا بنصرك إيانا، وأنت الذي تلي علينا أمورنا

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَآ
rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet received the closing verses of Baqara; angels urged him to ask, Gabriel taught this prayer, and Gabriel answered after each section that God had granted it.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل بن سليمان: لما أسري بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى السماء، أعطي خواتيم سورة البقرة

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَآ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God answers the prayer section by section: He will not hold them accountable or impose burdens, and has pardoned, forgiven, shown mercy, and granted victory.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس في قول الله عز وجل: {غفرانك ربنا} قال: قد غفرت لكم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says God placed this prayer of the Prophet and believers in scripture so later generations could preserve and frequently recite it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: هذا الدعاء أخبر الله عز وجل به عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمؤمنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested victory includes establishing the proof, prevailing in war and other affairs, and making the religion manifest over every religion as promised.
rows.anchor: انصرنا عليهم في إقامة الحجة، وفي غلبتنا إياهم في حربهم وسائر أمورهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says the address targets Jews who claimed to be God's beloved children and descendants of chosen prophets; God hears their ancestry claims and knows their denial of Muhammad despite recognizing his Torah description.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس (¬2): هذا مخاطبة لليهود الذين قالوا: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه،

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: One view says God hears what the chosen descendants say and knows what they conceal, preferring them because He knew their speech and conduct would be upright.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى: {والله سميع} لما تقوله (الذرية) المصطفاة {عليم} بما تضمره

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: A second view connects the verse to the following account: God hears the wife of Imran's words and knows her inward intention when she says her vow.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية تتصل بما بعدها، تقديرها: {والله سميع} لما تقوله امرأة عمران، {عليم} بما تضمره،

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats إذ as an idle extra with no grammatical position, so the sense is simply The wife of Imran said.
rows.anchor: فزعم أبو عبيدة (¬3) أنها زائدة، لغو؛ والمعنى: (قالت امرأة عمران)، ولا موضع لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects Abu Ubayda: a particle that indicates past time cannot be meaningless.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): ولم يصنع أبو عبيدة في هذا شيئا، لأن (إذ) تدل على ما مضى

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also rejects dropping the grammatical force of a Qur'anic particle when a meaningful analysis is available.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري (¬6) منكرا لهذا القول أيضا

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and Al-Mubarrad supply an omitted imperative: Remember when the wife of Imran said.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش، والمبرد (¬2): المعنى: (اذكر إذ قالت امرأة عمران).

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq makes the عامل of إذ the sense of God's choosing the family of Imran: He chose them when the wife of Imran said her vow.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق (¬4): المعنى عندي: (واصطفى آل عمران {إذ قالت امرأت عمران})

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr rejects Abu Ishaq's attachment: the choosing of Adam and Noah preceded the wife's statement, and this Imran differs from Imran father of Moses and Aaron by about 1,800 years.
rows.anchor: وأنكر أبو بكر هذا، وقال: الله تعالى قرن اصطفاءه [آل عمران] (¬7) باصطفائه آدم ونوحا

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Another view links this verse to the preceding description and takes إذ as governed by the sense of Hearing, Knowing.
rows.anchor: وذكرنا أيضا عن بعض أهل المعاني أن هذه الآية متصلة بما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran's wife was Hanne, Mary's mother and Jesus' grandmother; she vowed a child to service in the Jerusalem sanctuary in gratitude, reflecting a custom that children had to fulfill parents' vows of temple service.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {امرأت عمران} هي: حنة (¬4)، أم مريم، جدة عيسى عليه السلام، دعت الله أن يهب لها ولدا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhart means I imposed or obligated; a vow is something a person obligates himself to, conditionally or unconditionally.
rows.anchor: معنى {نذرت}: [أوجبت] (¬1). والنذر: ما يوجبه الإنسان على نفسه بشريطة كان، أو بغير شريطة

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Linguists explain a vow as warding off feared harm through a self-imposed good deed; its root is الإنذار, notifying someone of danger.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: معنى النذر: استدفاع المخوف، بما يعقد على النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarraran is a circumstantial accusative modifying ما, understood as the child in her womb in a state of consecration.
rows.anchor: وانتصب {محررا} على الحال من {ما} تقديره: نذرت لك الذي في بطني محررا (¬2)

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says she meant to make the child liberated and pure for God, serving the church and worship; muḥarrar denotes anything freed or purified, as in an emancipated slave, refined book, unattached free man, or clean clay.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة (¬3): أرادت نذرت لك أن أجعل (¬4) ما في بطني محررا، أي: عتيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptance means taking something with approval; the word derives from meeting or facing because the thing taken is met with recompense.
rows.anchor: معنى التقبل (¬1): أخذ الشيء على الرضى (¬2) به (¬3). وأصله، من: المقابلة؛ لأنه يقابل بالجزاء ما يؤخذ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is hearing her supplication and knowing what is in her heart.
rows.anchor: أي: لدعاي (¬4). {العليم} بما في قلبي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqabbala and qabula both mean to approve and accept; qabūl is used because it shares the meaning of taqabbul.
rows.anchor: التقبل، والقبول، معناهما سواء، وهو: أن ترضى بالشيء، وتأخذه؛

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Arabic can replace a verb's own verbal noun with another verbal noun of the same meaning despite differences in form, as in تكلمت كلاما; this is a verbal noun other than the expected one.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء (¬2): والعرب قد تترك المصدر للفعل المذكور، وتأتي بمصدر آخر في معنى الأول،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr says this is the only verbal noun on faʿūl with a fatḥa and that he had not heard it with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء (¬3): وليس في المصادر (فعول) بفتح الفاء،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh lists five verbal nouns on faʿūl: qabūl, wuḍūʾ, ṭahūr, walūʿ, and waqūd, though waqūd is more often with ḍamma as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه (¬1): خمسة (¬2) مصادر، جاءت على (فعول): (قبول)، و (وضوء) (¬3)، و (طهور)،

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj allow qabūl to be pronounced with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الفراء (¬6)، والزجاج (¬7) (قبولا) بالضم.

rows.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Thaʿlab, citing Ibn al-Aʿrabi, gives both pronunciations qabūlan and qabūlan and says the phrase على وجهه قبول is the only other usage; a poem witnesses the expression.
rows.anchor: ثعلب، عن ابن الأعرابي (¬8): يقال: قبلته (قبولا)، و (قبولا) (¬9)،

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say God accepted Mary in place of the consecrated male child Hanne had vowed, since no female had previously been accepted for that role.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬4): معنى قوله: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن} أي: رضيها مكان المحرر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Al-Dahhak's narration, explains the acceptance as setting Mary on the path of the blessed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك: معناه: سلك بها طريق السعداء.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says نباتا has a different form from أنبت but conveys that she grew well.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬1): جاء لفظ (¬2) {نباتا} على غير لفظ (أنبت)، على معنى: نبتت نباتا حسنا.

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the causative verb carries the sense of her growing herself; he supports meaning-based syntax with Imru al-Qays' line where رضت conveys أذللت.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري (¬3): لما كان (أنبت) يدل على [نبتت] (¬4) حمل (¬5) الفعل على المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, explains Mary's good growth as righteousness, knowledge of God, obedience, and service in the mosque.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬4)، في قوله: {وأنبتها نباتا حسنا}؛ يريد: في صلاح ومعرفة بالله،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Al-Dahhak, says she developed with balanced form, neither excess nor deficiency, growing in a day what a child grows in a year.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية الضحاك (¬5): يعنى: سوى خلقها من غير زيادة، ولا نقصان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed Mary in Zakariyya's care, and he assumed responsibility for her.
rows.anchor: أي: ضمها (¬1) إلى نفسه وقام بأمرها.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses the construction as undertaking her care; a kāfil is someone who takes a person in, supports, and pays for their maintenance.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬2): ومعناه في هذا: ضمن القيام بأمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya is nominative because the verb of assigning care is ascribed to him.
rows.anchor: و {زكريا}، رفع بفعله (¬7)، لأن الكفالة نسبت إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya has shortened and lengthened forms; both are indeclinable because they end in the feminine alif, whose fixed presence functions like two declension-blocking causes.
rows.anchor: وفيه قراءتان: القصر، والمد، وهما لغتان فيه،

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read with a doubled fāʾ, making Zakariyya accusative as the second object; the sense is that God entrusted her to him.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (وكفلها) مشددا، ومصدره: التكفيل، والتكفلة (¬8)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Mary was born, Hanne brought her to the Temple custodians as her vowed offering; the priests competed for her, cast lots, and the lot fell to Zakariyya.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن (حنة) لما ولدت مريم، أتت بها سدنة بيت المقدس،

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say Zakariyya built Mary a chamber in the mosque with a high entrance reached only by a ladder, and no one besides him ascended to it.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬1): لما ضم زكريا مريم إلى نفسه، بنى لها محرابا في المسجد، وبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrāb can mean the most honored assembly; Israelite miḥrābs were their places of worship.
rows.anchor: و (المحراب) في اللغة: أشرف المجالس. وكانت محاريب بني إسرائيل مساجدهم (¬2).

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says miḥrāb means a chamber, citing the verse about people scaling the miḥrāb in 38:21; Umar ibn Abi Rabiʿa's poem uses it likewise.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي (¬1): (المحراب): الغرفة؛ ألا تراه يقول: {إذ تسوروا المحراب} [سورة ص: 21].

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines miḥrāb as the highest room in a house or place in a mosque and says it means a chamber here.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬2): (المحراب): أرفع بيت في الدار، وأرفع مكان في المسجد،

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says miḥrāb is the leading, most honored assembly; a mosque's qibla and a palace are called miḥrāb because each is its foremost place.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة (¬4): (المحراب) عند العرب سيد المجالس، ومقدمها، وأشرفها،

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays uses the plural miḥārīb to mean palaces.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ (¬6) القيس: كغزلان وحش في محاريب أقوال (¬7)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says Mary had a chamber where she climbed to pray night and day.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬2): صارت عنده لها غرفة تصعد إليها تصلي فيها الليل والنهار.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Al-Rabiʿ say Mary found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, brought by angels from Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال (¬3) ابن عباس (¬4)، والربيع (¬5): كان زكريا كلما دخل عليها غرفتها وجد عندها رزقا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says this provision occurred after Mary had reached adulthood.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق (¬1): كان هذا كله، بعد أن بلغت مريم مبلغ النساء.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it happened in Mary's infancy: she never nursed, received food from Paradise, and spoke as a child when answering Zakariyya.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬2): كان هذا في صغرها، ولم ترضع ثديا قط، بل (¬3) كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة،

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq makes كلما accusative through وجد; ما with دخل acts like the verbal noun, meaning every time of entering the chamber.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬5): ونصب {كلما} بقوله: {وجد} (¬6)؛ أي: يجد عندها الرزق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses this as Where did this come from? Zakariyya asked to ensure the provision came from God rather than another person.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): يريد: من أين لك هذا؟ وإنما سألها؛ لأنه خاف أن يأتيها الرزق من غير جهته،

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement may be Mary's continuation or a new sentence; the author prefers a new sentence because it does not answer Zakariyya's question.
rows.anchor: وهذا يحتمل أن يكون من كلام مريم، ويحتمل أنه على (¬5) الابتداء، والأولى به الاستئناف (¬6)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to the account just told about Zakariyya, Mary, and Yahya.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى ما قص من حديث زكريا، ومريم، ويحيى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy means conveying a message to someone by messenger, inspiration, writing, or gesture; Qur'anic examples include revelation to Muhammad, inspiration to bees and Moses' mother, a gesture by Zakariyya, and satanic whispering.
rows.anchor: الإيحاء) في اللغة: إلقاء معنى الكلام إلى من تريد إعلامه؛ إما بإرسال رسول، أو بإلهام، أو بكتابة، أو بإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqlām is the plural of qalam, from cutting: a writing pen is sharpened at its tip, and a lot arrow is cut at both ends.
rows.anchor: و (القلم) (¬2) أصله من: (القلم)، وهو: قطع للطرف (¬3)،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says prophets disputed over Mary's custody; after invoking God and casting their arrows into a spring, Zakariyya's arrow floated while the rest sank, and he won the lot.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬1): هؤلاء كانوا جماعة من الأنبياء، اختلفوا واختصموا في مريم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they were marked lottery arrows used to identify who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬8): هي قداح جعلوا عليها علامات، يعرفون بها من يكفل مريم على جهة القرعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is elliptical: they cast lots to determine which of them would be assigned Mary's care.
rows.anchor: مختصر (¬1)؛ أي: لينظروا أيهم تجب له كفالة مريم (¬2).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ links this sentence to the previous one and marks sequence, giving the sense: after taking the covenant, do they seek another religion? A wāw could link them but would not mark sequence.
rows.anchor: دخلت الفاء في {أفغير} لأنه عطف جملة على جملة (¬5)، وكذلك (¬6) لو قيل: (أوغير)، إلا أن الفاء ترتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ reading follows the preceding direct address, including Have you affirmed and taken the covenant?
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بالتاء (¬8)؛ فلأن ما قبله خطاب؛ كقوله: {أأقررتم وأخذتم}.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading treats the statement as God's report of the Jews, Christians, and others who disbelieved after the covenant, in a condemnatory question.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء (¬1)؛ فوجهه: أن الله تعالى أخبر في الآية السابقة، عن أخذ الميثاق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads يبغون with yāʾ but ترجعون with tāʾ because the first is specifically about Jews and others while the return concerns all legally responsible people.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: {يبغون} بالياء، و {ترجعون} بالتاء (¬3)؛ لأن الأول: خاص لليهود (¬4)

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet explained the verse as angels obeying God in heaven and ʿAbd al-Qays obeying Him on earth.
rows.anchor: روى (¬7) أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، قال في هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas through Ata, also followed by Al-Hasan, identifies heavenly people as angels and earthly willing submitters as emigrants, Helpers, and ʿAbd al-Qays, with the rest submitting unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وبهذا (¬1)؛ قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬2): قال: يريد بأهل السموات: الملائكة. وبأهل الأرض:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says believers submit willingly and benefit from acceptance, whereas disbelievers submit under compulsion at the onset of punishment and death, when faith no longer helps, as in 40:85.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة (¬4): المؤمن، أسلم طائعا فنفعه (¬5) ذلك، وقبل منه، والكافر، أسلم كرها في وقت البأس

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان والزجاج
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan and Al-Zajjaj say all submit through their created nature and God's ordering, which none can resist or change; return to God confirms He began and will resurrect people by His will, whether they choose it or not.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان (¬1)، والزجاج (¬2): أي: خضعوا وانقادوا من جهة ما فطرهم عليه، ودبرهم به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is a threat: people who abandon God's religion for another will return to Him and be repaid for rejecting His religion.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: {وإليه يرجعون} وعيد لهم؛ أي: أتبغون غير دين الله، وتزيغون عن الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawʿ means yielding: ṭāʿa is to obey or submit, while ṭāwaʿa is to agree with someone.
rows.anchor: الطوع: الانقياد؛ يقال: (طاعه، يطوعه، طوعا) (¬5): إذا انقاد له، وخضع.

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit treats ṭāʿa lahu and aṭāʿahu as equivalent, giving two conjugations: ṭāʿa yaṭūʿu and ṭāʿa yuṭāʿu.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت (¬1): يقال: (طاع له، وأطاعه)، سواء، فمن قال: (طاع)، قال: (يطاع)،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusatives are verbal nouns functioning as circumstantial states, meaning willing or unwilling; أتاني ركضا works as I came running, unlike أتاني كلاما, since speech is not a mode of arrival.
rows.anchor: وانتصب {طوعا وكرها}؛ على أنه مصدر وقع موقع الحال؛ وتقديره: طائعا (¬2) أو كارها (¬3)؛

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid and Muqatil restrict God's easing to allowing marriage to a female slave in cases of necessity.
rows.anchor: فقال: المراد به نكاح الأمة عند الضرورة. وهو قول مجاهد (¬1) ومقاتل (¬2).

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The broader view includes all legal rulings and whatever God makes easy as a kindness, contrasting with the burdens placed on the Children of Israel; Ibn Abbas explains that God eases severe obligations.
rows.anchor: وعلى العموم دل كلام ابن عباس في تفسيره هذا التخفيف فقال: يريد شدة المئونة يخففها عنكم (¬3).
